title: Evaluation of the normalized system coefficient mate
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism, $c$ a compactification, $\ell\in\mathbf N$, and $t:\operatorname{Theory}(c,\ell)$ a normalized ordinary system presentation [def-pur-etale-system-projection-data]. For finite $\ell$-power-torsion coefficient sequences $B_\bullet,C_\bullet$, a compatible coefficient map $a:B_\bullet\to C_\bullet$, a level $n$, and any unbounded derived strict system $M$ on $X$, evaluation of $q_a$ transported through the specified support and scalar evaluation isomorphisms is exactly the published $C_n$-linear compact-support scalar map $\operatorname{compactScalarMap}(a_n,c)$ on $e_nM$. The equation is the five-factor transport word in the attached Lean statement, not merely an identification of its source and target.

source.place: Tag 0GL6, remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings; Zheng Constructions 4.1, 5.14-5.15 and Lemma 5.16. Agent elaboration of Original item proof steps 3-4: scalar and geometric transpose calculation, then level evaluation.

proof.text: Apply the proved etaleSingleCoefficientProjection at B_n and C_n, using the finite and torsion fields of B and C. Obtain the canonical restriction isomorphism d, its forward-map equation and the transpose formula for compactScalarMap. The unit characterization of mates identifies the mate of compactScalarMap with d.inv.

The normalization fields ScalarEvaluation.mate identify the mates of the inverse scalar evaluation isomorphisms with the forward restriction evaluation isomorphisms. The definition of projection identifies the mate of q with RestrictionSupport.iso.inv. Apply etaleSystemRestriction_evaluation to d to supply the restriction cube.

Apply CategoryTheory.mateEquiv_app_cube_converse to the system scalar adjunctions on X and Y and the single-ring scalar adjunctions on X and Y. The four mate identifications give its right-adjoint cube hypothesis. Its conclusion is the three-factor scalar evaluation cube. Postcompose with the forward support evaluation at scalarX(M) and compact support applied to the forward scalar evaluation on X. Functoriality and inverse/hom cancellation turn that cube into the original five-factor equation.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GL6; reuse of the proved single-ring normalization, restriction evaluation, and the converse cube-of-mates identity in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.MateCube.

theorem etaleSystemProjection_evaluation
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} (c : Compactification f) (l : ℕ) (t : Theory c l) :
    (∀ (B C : Coefficients.{u} l) (a : B.rings ⟶ C.rings) (n : ℕ)
        (M : Derived X B.rings),
        (scalarExtension (a.app (op n)).hom Y).map
            ((t.supportEvaluation B n).iso.inv.app M) ≫
          (t.scalarEvaluationY a n).iso.inv.app ((t.support B).F.obj M) ≫
          (t.evaluationY C n).E.map ((t.q a).app M) ≫
          (t.supportEvaluation C n).iso.hom.app ((t.scalarX a).model.T.obj M) ≫
          (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification
            (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (C.rings.obj (op n))) c).map
              ((t.scalarEvaluationX a n).iso.hom.app M) =
          (compactScalarMap (a.app (op n)).hom c).app ((t.evaluationX B n).E.obj M))
